name: manifest_db
description: List an iOS backup's map: for each file id in Manifest.db its domain, relative path, kind, the metadata of its keyed archive (size, mode, owner, protection class, inode, three times) and the state of the blob the id names (present, missing, a directory, a link never followed, not applicable, or refused). It does not rebuild a file system, open or decrypt a payload, or read a password. It reads the backup's plain files (Manifest.plist, Info.plist, Status.plist) for the encryption flag, the device, the backup's version and date and its completion state. Encryption is three-valued: encrypted, not_encrypted, or unknown (Manifest.plist missing, unreadable or without IsEncrypted: never read as unencrypted). An encrypted backup is never reported as empty: when Manifest.db opens as SQLite its rows are listed with payload_encrypted true; when it does not, the answer says the listing is not available and what the file was. No decryption is provided by this tool or this pack. SENSITIVE: key material in Manifest.plist (the key bag, the manifest key) is reported as present with its length and never printed, hashed or previewed, and a path component shaped like a recovery password is withheld from every path; the tool writes no values file. Times are NOT guessed: epoch (unix by default, or apple) is applied to every time, the raw seconds are returned beside the ISO 8601 UTC time, and the earliest and latest value read are in the answer so that a wrong epoch shows as a range of decades; check the epoch against a file whose time the case documents. Metadata comes from the keyed archive's root ($top.root, followed through UID references with a depth bound and a cycle check), not from the first object with a Size. A file id is validated (40 hexadecimal digits) before it is joined to a path, and the path must stay inside the backup; both the sharded layout (<xx>/<id>) and the flat one are looked for. A -wal or -journal beside Manifest.db is copied with it to a working directory under $OUT and opened there, never the original. The whole listing is kept: the inline page is limit rows and the rest is in the file the answer names. status is complete, or partial (the listing is not available, or the time limit stopped it).

path.description: The backup directory, or its Manifest.db

contains.description: Case-insensitive regex over the relative path (at most 1000 characters)

domain.description: Only this domain exactly, e.g. HomeDomain or AppDomain-com.example

epoch.description: unix (default) or apple: the epoch the file times are counted from. Never inferred; check it against a file whose time the case documents

limit.description: Entries (and domains) in the inline answer (default 200, and at most 1 MiB of rows); the whole list is in the file the answer names

max_seconds.description: Stop reading rows after this long (default 240); the answer says partial and where it stopped
